title: Self Employed: 5 Things I learned that NOBODY tells you
summary: Self-employed creator's five lessons: earning is harder, time management, isolation, taxes and insurance, and doing every job yourself.

assertions.quote: making a dollar working for yourself is way harder than making a dollar when you're working for somebody else

verdicts.note: Most new businesses take years to match a prior salary; many never do.

After controls the median self-employed earns about 15% less per hour than a comparable salaried worker and the median unincorporated owner about 30% less (the bottom quartile 51% less), while working more hours; but incorporated owners earn more than employees, and the paper does not measure time to break even.

assertions.quote: always having about two years in savings or three years in savings is even better

verdicts.note: Runway advice is sensible; the right length varies by business.

assertions.quote: being self-employed you kind of have to drive your own schedule and be accountable and that can be really hard for some people

verdicts.note: Surveys of the self-employed consistently report isolation and self-discipline as top challenges.

assertions.quote: you have to budget for taxes on your own social security taxes can actually make up a large portion of your tax bill

verdicts.note: Self-employment tax covers both halves of payroll tax and no employer subsidizes insurance.

assertions.quote: they should outsource all the things that they're not super good at
there's definitely a tax on your mental state when you're switching consistently from you know one topic to another

verdicts.note: Task-switching costs are documented in cognitive research; the business effect is anecdotal.
